chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: We discuss and say that whoever performs salat (prayer) while sitting without an illness, his salat is counted as two rakʿahs for one rakʿah, and two sajdahs for one sajdah. So he said: It is not like that; it is complete for you.

key_terms.جَالِسٌ: sitting; describing the posture of the worshipper during salat (prayer)
key_terms.هَكَذَا: in this manner; referring to the claimed ruling

ai.seo_question: Is a supererogatory prayer performed while sitting without illness considered complete in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on performing salat (prayer) while seated without an excuse, specifically in the context of supererogatory prayers. Imam Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام rejects the claim that such a prayer is reduced in value or counted fractionally, and states that it is complete for the worshipper.
